chapter: Clarifications and portraits: Lester Young, Byas, Blanton, Ben Webster
title: Time in Chicago, Mosby's wife's club and the Big Apple on Central Avenue
summary: He was in Chicago 1937-41; more about Mosby's clubs and other Central Avenue spots.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: How long were you in Chicago before you went to New York?
Oh, and you said that Curtis Mosby's wife --
Oh, let's see, I'm sorry, I went there in '37 and I left February of '41. So three years and a couple of months.
-- you mentioned that Curtis Mosby's wife ran one of the Clubs on Central Avenue in Los Angeles. Do you remember what her name was?
No, I don't. Oh, all I knew was Mrs. Mosby.
Was she an entertainer at all?
Not that I know of. She may a -- have been. The Club's name was the "Last Word".
It was the "Last Word," the "Downbeat," the mo. Those were the names of all the Clubs?

And then later they had a little band after my mother had tricked me back out here from Chicago in '38. They had a band, a place up around 42nd and Third called the "Big Apple". It was primarily a billiard parlor and they empty

it out and made a sort of nightery out of it. But it wasn't a night club in the true sense. Like they had a bar, you know, with a rail you can put your foot on, a band and a dance floor. That was all. No show.
How about Brother's was the after hours part upstairs on Central Avenue, was that operating?
Brother's After Hours Club, yes that was operating.
